source_documents.title: Enhancement of intersystem crossing in asymmetrically substituted BODIPY photosensitizers

reference_evidence_units.quote: For instance, aBDP4 displayed a FD value of 47% in cyclohexane.
reference_evidence_units.subject: aBDP4
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Singlet oxygen yield is an indirect measure of triplet formation.

reference_evidence_units.quote: In contrast, compounds with nearly degenerate S1 and T2 levels (i.e., DES1–T2 values of ca. 0.1 eV, such as aBDP3, aBDP4, and aBDP14) should enhance the S1 - T2 ISC process. As a result, intermediate FD values ranging from 21% to 47% are observed for these compounds in apolar solvents.
reference_evidence_units.subject: aBDP4
reference_evidence_units.statement: S1 and T2 are nearly degenerate in aBDP4, opening S1-to-T2 ISC.

reference_evidence_units.quote: We conclude that the S1 - T2 ISC process should be the main ISC process for these compounds.
reference_evidence_units.subject: aBDPs
reference_evidence_units.statement: S1-to-T2 is the main ISC channel in the asymmetrical dyes.

reference_evidence_units.quote: However, attempts to detect phosphorescence for aBDPs were unsuccessful (Fig. S27, ESI†), indicating that their triplet states are subject to rapid nonradiative decay under these conditions.
reference_evidence_units.subject: aBDPs
reference_evidence_units.statement: No phosphorescence; triplet formation is inferred from singlet oxygen only.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The introduction of an ethoxycarbonyl group on one of the rings further enhances this effect, which can be attributed to an asymmetric charge distribution between the pyrrolic rings, reducing the aromaticity and increasing non-radiative decays.
reference_evidence_units.subject: aBDPs with one ester ring
reference_evidence_units.statement: Fluorescence yield falls (aBDP4: 0.47 in CYH to 0.07 in ACN) because asymmetric charge distribution raises nonradiative decay.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The very low FD values of approximately 5% measured for the symmetrical sBDP1 and sBDP2 are consistent with the thermodynamically uphill S1 - T2 ISC process (T2 being 0.25 eV above S1, see Table 3).
reference_evidence_units.subject: sBDP2
reference_evidence_units.statement: sBDP2: singlet oxygen yield 0.02-0.03; T2 lies 0.25 eV above S1.

reference_evidence_units.quote: while preserving high fluorescence quantum yields
reference_evidence_units.subject: sBDP2
reference_evidence_units.statement: sBDP2 fluoresces with Phi_Fl 0.92-0.97 in all four solvents (Table 1).

reference_mechanisms.label: RADIATIVE_RATE_STATE_BALANCE
reference_mechanisms.rationale: The fall of fluorescence yield with polarity is assigned to higher nonradiative decay from the asymmetric charge distribution.

reference_mechanisms.label: TRIPLET_ISC_RTP_TADF
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Heavy-atom-free ISC enabled by the asymmetric substitution: S1-to-T2 near-degeneracy (computed) and singlet oxygen yield up to 0.47 in non-polar solvents. Triplets are inferred from singlet oxygen only (no phosphorescence, no transient absorption).

mechanism_decisions.label: RIM_RIR_RIV
mechanism_decisions.rationale: Not discussed for this molecule in the source.

mechanism_decisions.label: ICT_TICT_CT
mechanism_decisions.rationale: The paper reports negative solvatochromism (ground state more polar than S1) and CT character of T2, but does not assign the emission to an ICT state.

contrast_group.varied_factor: symmetric vs asymmetric pyrrole substitution of the BODIPY core (2,6-diester tetramethyl vs one 5-ester ring and one 1,3-dimethyl-2-ethyl ring)
contrast_group.paper_difference: The symmetrical diester sBDP2 is a bright fluorophore with singlet oxygen yield about 0.03 (T2 0.25 eV above S1); asymmetrical aBDP4 has nearly degenerate S1/T2, singlet oxygen yield up to 0.47 in cyclohexane and much lower fluorescence.
